name: 80 mm robot joint actuator, 100:1
summary: An integrated joint with a frameless motor, strain wave gear, dual encoders and an EtherCAT driver, for arm shoulders and humanoid hips. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

demand.reason: India installed a record number of industrial robots in 2024, and makers are automating to meet export quality demands. Many humanoid developers buy tested joint modules instead of building their own, and joints in the 50 to 150 Nm class are the largest share in 2026.

parts.name: Rear cover
parts.role: Close the back of the joint and carry the cable gland.
parts.whatItDoes: An aluminium cap that seals the electronics end and holds the power and bus cable entry.
parts.whyItMatters: The cable entry is where joints let in dust and fluid. A good gland keeps the encoder clean.
buyingChecks: Ask for the ingress rating of the closed joint
Check the cable gland suits your cable diameter
Ask whether the cover can be removed without breaking a seal

parts.name: Motor driver board
parts.role: Turn bus commands into motor currents.
parts.whatItDoes: A round board with the power stage, current sensors and a processor that runs the field-oriented control loop and talks over EtherCAT or CAN.
parts.whyItMatters: The driver decides how smooth and quiet the joint is at low speed, and it is where most of the heat outside the motor is made.
parts.material: FR-4 board with power MOSFETs and processor
buyingChecks: Ask which bus is supported: EtherCAT, CAN or both
Ask for the control loop rate
Ask for the processor and MOSFET makers and origin

parts.name: Encoder
parts.whatItDoes: A code disc on the motor shaft read by a sensor head. Many joints add a second encoder on the output to see through gear wind-up.
parts.whyItMatters: Encoder resolution and accuracy set how precisely the robot can position its tool or foot.
parts.material: Glass or metal code disc with optical or magnetic read head
buyingChecks: Ask for the encoder resolution in bits and its accuracy
Ask whether there is an output-side encoder
Ask for the encoder maker and origin

parts.name: Frameless stator
parts.role: Make the rotating magnetic field that drives the joint.
parts.whatItDoes: A wound steel lamination stack bonded inside the housing. Frameless means it has no case or bearings of its own.
parts.whyItMatters: Winding quality and lamination thickness set torque per amp and heat. The stator is the joint's main heat source.
parts.material: Silicon steel laminations with copper windings
buyingChecks: Ask for torque constant and winding resistance
Ask for lamination thickness and steel grade
Ask for the insulation class of the windings

parts.name: Magnet rotor
parts.role: Carry the magnets that the stator field pulls around.
parts.whatItDoes: A steel hub with rare-earth magnets bonded on its outside, running inside the stator with a small air gap.
parts.whyItMatters: Magnet grade and temperature rating set torque and how hot the joint can run. Magnet origin is often undocumented.
buyingChecks: Ask for the magnet grade and maximum temperature
Ask in writing where the magnets are made
Ask how the magnets are retained at speed

parts.name: Wave generator
parts.role: Flex the gear spline in a rotating wave.
parts.whatItDoes: An elliptical cam with a thin flexible ball bearing on it, driven by the motor rotor. It pushes the flexspline into an oval that turns with the motor.
parts.whyItMatters: The bearing on the cam carries every gear load. It is the life-limiting part of the gear.
parts.material: Hardened steel cam with thin-section ball bearing
buyingChecks: Ask for the rated life of the wave generator bearing
Ask for the lubricant and relube interval
Ask whether the gear set is from a named gear maker

parts.name: Flexspline
parts.role: Carry the output and mesh with the ring gear.
parts.whatItDoes: A thin steel cup with fine teeth around its rim. The wave generator flexes it so its teeth engage the ring gear two places at a time.
parts.whyItMatters: This is the gear's reduction: two teeth fewer than the ring gear gives ratios like 100 to 1 with almost no backlash. Fatigue of the cup limits peak torque.
buyingChecks: Ask for repeated peak torque and momentary peak torque ratings
Ask for backlash and lost motion in arc-seconds
Ask for the steel grade and heat treatment

parts.name: Circular spline
parts.role: Hold the fixed ring of teeth the flexspline walks around.
parts.whatItDoes: A rigid steel ring with internal teeth, bolted to the housing.
parts.whyItMatters: Ring accuracy sets how smooth the output is. Poor ring teeth show up as torque ripple at the tool.
buyingChecks: Ask for the gear accuracy grade
Check the ring is pinned as well as bolted
Ask whether ring and flexspline come as a matched set

parts.name: Cross-roller bearing
parts.role: Carry the load on the output, in every direction.
parts.whatItDoes: A bearing with rollers set at alternating right angles, so one bearing takes radial, axial and tilting loads.
parts.whyItMatters: The output bearing decides how much bending load the joint can take before it deflects or wears.
buyingChecks: Ask for the rated tilting moment
Ask for the bearing maker
Ask for the preload setting

parts.name: Output flange
parts.role: Bolt the next link of the robot to the joint.
parts.whatItDoes: A machined plate on the front of the joint with a bolt circle and dowel holes for the next arm link.
parts.whyItMatters: Flange flatness and the dowel fit decide how accurately the next link is located.
buyingChecks: Check the bolt circle and dowel pattern against your link
Ask for flatness of the flange face
Ask for the maximum bolt torque

parts.name: Housing
parts.role: Hold everything in line and carry heat out of the stator.
parts.whatItDoes: A machined aluminium tube that the stator is bonded into and the ring gear bolts to. Its outside is the joint's cooling surface.
parts.whyItMatters: Housing stiffness keeps the gear in line under load. Its thermal path decides how long the joint can hold rated torque.
buyingChecks: Ask for the continuous torque rating and the housing temperature at that rating
Ask for the alloy and surface finish
Check the mounting pattern against your structure
